newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish O/N depos soar above 25 pct lombard rate.
newsitem.headline: Polish O/N depos soar above 25 pct lombard rate.

text.p: Polish overnight deposits soared to above lombard rate levels as the market found itself out of cash on Friday -- the last trading day of the monthly reserve.
Dealers said some banks had larger cash needs than their lombard rate limit and had to seach for cash on the market above the central bank's 25 percent lombard rate.
"O/N rates topped the lombard rate as banks search the market for cash they can't get from the central bank at 25 percent," said Marek Wieczorkiewicz, chief dealer at PKO BP.
At 0840 GMT, O/N rates were quoted at 25.0/26.50 percent, up from 23.0/25.6 percent at 0630 GMT and Thursday's 20.0/22.0.
"Banks' needs are so large, that they are taking in cash at above 25 percent," said Violetta Gorecka of PKO SA.

Dealers said larger than expected end-of-month outflows created a hole in Polish banks' required reserve accounts on Thursday and today's 269 million zloty net inflow in to the system was not large enough balance the required accounts.
The September reserve period ends on Sunday.

"Banks are afraid that large end-of-month outflows will continue at this afternoon's clearing session and want to make sure their reserve requirements are secure so that they don't pay any fines," one Polish bank dealer said.
Tomorrow/next rates were quoted at 20.00/21.50 percent, relatively flat from 20.3/22.3 percent on Thursday.

On the forex market the Polish zloty inched down against the basket of currencies in light early trade to about 1.78/1.74 percent from the trading band centre from 1.84/1.76 percent at 0710 GMT and 1.80/1.71 percent on Thursday.
At 0900 GMT the zloty was at 2.8035/45 to the dollar, down from 2.8020/40 at opening and 2.8025/45 on Thursday.
It was at 1.8410/20 to the mark, down from opening's 1.8400/15 and nearly flat from yesterday's 1.8405/25.

Dealers said today's statement by Polish Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko, who said that the zloty rate would weaken to 3.07 per dollar by September 1997 did not have any immidiate effect on the forex market.
A recent Reuter poll of the country's 26 top banks showed that dealers expected the dollar/zloty exchange rate 12 months ahead, in September 1997, at 3.04 zlotys.
